readme.html:
Awesome Copilot Office Skills

Draw, tidy and check decks and workbooks inside Copilot in PowerPoint and Excel. 27 skills: build diagrams from your own content as editable shapes, strip the AI tone out of slide text, check a deck makes one argument, and audit a workbook before it goes out. Every one drafts and stops for your approval. Upload a zip, drop a folder in OneDrive, or have IT deploy them. The same SKILL.md files also run in Claude, ChatGPT and Codex, GitHub Copilot and VS Code, Gemini CLI and Mistral Vibe.

This is a community library, not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft. Every vendor claim below names its source and the date it was read (24 October 2026). Anything not documented is marked Unconfirmed.

Try one in 60 seconds

PowerPoint: download executive-summary-slide.zip, then Copilot pane > + > Choose skills > Manage skills > Add skill > upload. Type @executive-summary-slide add a summary slide.

Excel: download reconciliation-check.zip and unzip it, then Copilot pane > Settings > Manage plugins & skills > Custom skills > Open skills folder > copy the folder in > Refresh. Type @reconciliation-check does this pack tie out? Your Office display language must be English.

Full lists with what each one does: Excel and PowerPoint. A worked session that chains several together: the tutorial.

Contents: Install · Excel catalog · PowerPoint catalog · Other tools · Limits · FAQ · Tested status

Two rules behind every file

  • Prompts are the asset, models are commodities. A skill is a text file you own. It outlives the model and the vendor, so it is written once in an open format and run wherever you work.
  • AI prepares, people decide. Each skill drafts, shows you what it would change, and waits. Nothing is applied, approved or decided until a person says so. Reconciliation breaks stay breaks until you resolve them, decision slides keep a blank outcome field, and scenario cases ship empty.

What a Copilot skill is (60 seconds)

A skill is a folder containing one file, SKILL.md: a short header with a name and a description telling Copilot when to use it, then plain instructions. Both apps discover skills from a Skills folder in your OneDrive, and both skip any folder whose name does not match the name inside the file. You call one directly with @skill-name, or Copilot picks an enabled skill when your request matches its description.

Surface Where skills come from Since Source
Copilot in Excel, custom skills You, via OneDrive or @skill-builder Announced 25 June 2026, Support page updated October 2026 Copilot in Excel: Built for the era of Frontier Finance; Use skills with Copilot in Excel
Copilot in Excel, Microsoft skills Microsoft: @brandkit, @chart-design, @clean-data, @skill-builder, @theme-design October 2026 Skills created by Microsoft
Copilot in PowerPoint, personal skills You, by upload, paste or OneDrive folder July to August 2026 Use custom skills with Copilot in PowerPoint; MC1434580, MC1441645
Copilot in PowerPoint, Record a Skill You, by demonstration October 2026 Record a skill; MC1490903
Copilot in PowerPoint, organization skills Your Microsoft 365 admin Frontier August 2026; Windows general availability September 2026 Deploy organization skills; MC1463509 (Frontier), MC1478961 (Windows), MC1478960 (Mac)
Copilot in Excel, organization skills Your Microsoft 365 admin Unconfirmed No Microsoft page documents it as of 24 October 2026. See runtimes/excel-organization.md

Both Microsoft pages say custom skills "must follow the industry standard format" and link the Agent Skills specification. That standard was donated by Anthropic to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation on 22 October 2026, after what Anthropic says was adoption by more than 70 agent platforms (Anthropic, Linux Foundation). That is why one folder runs in Excel, in PowerPoint and in half a dozen tools that are not Microsoft's.

Not the same thing: skills attached to a declarative agent in Agent Builder, and skills in Copilot Chat and Cowork. Same file format, different surfaces, different install paths. See runtimes/.

Install

Excel, personal skill (no admin)

  1. Download a zip from dist/personal/ and unzip it, or download this repository (Code > Download ZIP) and extract it outside OneDrive. Excel has no Add skill upload: you copy the folder in, so the zip is only a delivery wrapper.
  2. In Excel, open Copilot, select Settings (...) > Manage plugins & skills > Custom skills > Create OneDrive folder, then Open skills folder.
  3. Copy the skill folder in with its name unchanged, then select Refresh.
  4. Type @reconciliation-check (or any skill name) followed by your request.

🔴 Your Microsoft Office display language must be set to English, or skills do not appear in Excel at all. This is the most common reason a correctly built skill is invisible (Use skills with Copilot in Excel).

PowerPoint, personal skill (no admin)

  1. Download a zip from dist/personal/, or download this repository and extract it outside OneDrive.
  2. In PowerPoint, open Copilot, select + > Choose skills, scroll to Manage skills (labelled Manage plugins & skills in newer builds) and select Add skill. Upload the zip, or paste the contents of SKILL.md into the form.
  3. Or use the folder route: Settings (...) > Manage skills > Custom skills > Create OneDrive folder > Open skills folder, copy the folder in, then select Refresh.
  4. Type @outline-first-deck followed by your request.

Personal skills are visible only to you.

Record a Skill (PowerPoint, your own routine)

For a formatting routine you repeat, Copilot can draft a skill from what you do: Manage plugins & skills > Custom skills > Add skill > Record Skill, perform the task, select Stop, review the drafted instructions, then Upload. In Excel the equivalent is @skill-builder, which drafts a skill from your instructions, previous prompts or a completed workflow.

Organisation-wide (admin)

Microsoft documents this path for PowerPoint. Whether the same package reaches Copilot in Excel is Unconfirmed. Your admin builds packages with python3 scripts/build-dist (manifest version 1.30 with an agentSkills array, plus two icons) and uploads them in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > All agents > Add agent, targeting all users or chosen groups. Full guide: org-deploy/README.md.

These skills sit next to the built-ins rather than replacing them, and two of them overlap a built-in on purpose. PowerPoint's Agent mode already rewrites, translates and adds speaker notes (MC1243550, March 2026); speaker-notes-builder adds what that does not, namely gap markers where a note would need a fact the deck lacks, a contradiction check against existing notes, and timing against a slot. Excel ships Microsoft-managed skills (@brandkit, @clean-data, @skill-builder, @theme-design, and @chart-design which is off by default) and a set of built-in finance skills including check-model, which audits financial models for circular references, broken formulas, hardcoded overrides and imbalances (Skills created by Microsoft, read 24 October 2026). formula-risk-review, model-map and reconciliation-check cover the same ground on any workbook rather than on financial models, report only and never edit, and each stops at a human approval checkpoint. data-quality-sweep reports and quantifies; @clean-data proposes corrections.

Status, 24 October 2026: all 24 are format-validated by scripts/validate. Live tenant tests are pending. STATUS.md tracks what has actually been run, by surface, and lists the twelve open questions worth testing.

Same file, other tools

The skills are written host-neutral. Where a tool can edit the open file, the skill edits it after approval; where it cannot, the skill returns its output as Markdown to paste.

Tool Where the folder goes Page

Each folder is kept to name and description in the header, instructions under 20,000 characters (the strictest documented Microsoft limit) and text-only references, so one file passes every runtime's loader. Live behaviour outside the Microsoft 365 apps is not yet tested.

Does running a skill here spend Copilot Credits?

The honest answer is that Microsoft has not published one, and that is worth more to you than a confident guess. Here is exactly what is and is not documented, read on 25 October 2026.

What Microsoft does document

  • Cowork is billed in Copilot Credits. Credits are a real metered layer with a real meter behind them: the Cost Management API governs tenant credit consumption, caps it with spending policies, and reports per-user, per-service balances (Cost Management API overview).
  • A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence covers things a Copilot Chat account pays for. Microsoft's own pricing FAQ: "Copilot Chat customers may also use custom agents built by their organization on a metered basis", and "Licensed users can use assistive custom agents at no additional cost" (Microsoft Copilot plans and pricing).
  • The skills pages mention cost nowhere. Neither Use custom skills with Copilot in PowerPoint nor the Excel equivalent says anything about credits, metering or consumption.

What is not documented, and we will not fill in

That FAQ sentence is about agents. A custom skill in PowerPoint is not an agent, and no Microsoft page states whether running one draws on credits. So the structure makes it plausible that a licensed user running a skill in PowerPoint is inside their seat rather than on the meter, and plausible is not documented. We will not claim it.

If you are choosing where to run something because of cost, the thing to do is measure it, not read it here: the Cost Management API reports per-user, per-service balances, so a tenant admin can answer this for your tenant in an afternoon. If you do, please tell us and we will publish it with your name on it.

Why people move a skill from Cowork to PowerPoint anyway

Credits are one reason and not the only one. A skill that runs in the app keeps the file in front of you, edits the open deck directly, and needs no separate surface. If you have a Cowork skill you want to move, runtimes/cowork-to-powerpoint.md covers what changes.

Licensing

  • You need Copilot in the app. Microsoft's licence page: a Copilot Chat (Basic) account has no Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint or OneNote; M365 Copilot (Basic) has standard access in the apps; M365 Copilot (Premium) has the add-on licence with priority access (What Copilot license do I have, updated April 2026).
  • Unconfirmed: whether custom skills work on M365 Copilot (Basic), in either app. No page states the tier for custom skills.
  • Organization skills need a Microsoft 365 admin who can publish in the admin center.

Skill not showing up?

In order of how often it is the cause: your Office display language is not English (Excel only); the folder name does not match the name inside SKILL.md; you did not select Refresh after editing in OneDrive; or the zip shape is wrong, which is why both shapes ship. Longer answers in FAQ.md.

Known limits

  • Folder name must equal name, or the skill is skipped. This is documented for both apps.
  • Excel is English only. Your Office display language must be English.
  • ZIP uploads: PNG, PDF and nested zips are not supported. This repo ships text only.
  • Excel's documentation permits scripts, references and assets subfolders. This repository deliberately ships no scripts, so that one folder is safe to drop into either app and into every runtime above, and so nothing here executes on your machine.
  • Edit files in OneDrive, then select Refresh in Custom skills.
  • Unconfirmed: whether Excel and PowerPoint read the same OneDrive Skills folder or two separate ones, whether PowerPoint reads files in references/, whether optional header fields such as license are tolerated, the zip shape PowerPoint expects, and the maximum number of skills per user in either app.

Contributing

Read CONTRIBUTING.md, and start from templates/SKILL.template.md and templates/README.template.md. In short: one folder per skill directly under skills/, a surface entry in scripts/catalog.json, a header with exactly name and description (quoted), the nine required sections including a human approval checkpoint, no scripts or images, British spelling, no em dashes, and python3 scripts/validate must pass. Tenant reports, including things that worked, are the most useful contribution: use the issue template.

Sibling repositories

  • awesome-copilot-cowork-skills: folder-drop skills for Copilot Cowork.
  • awesome-copilot-agent-skills: skills for declarative agents in Agent Builder.
  • awesome-microsoft-copilot-prompts: single-message prompts.
  • awesome-mistral-vibe-skills: Agent Skills for Mistral Vibe.

From the same author

  • The Real Cost of Copilot, sample
  • Copilot Deployment Kit

Store pages carry their own terms, separate from this repository's licence.
